title: A cipher page in Cardinal Luigi d'Este's cipher, Rome 1584-85 (BnF Cinq Cents de Colbert 338, p. 523): read in part with Tomokiyo's key

steps.what: Tomokiyo's d'Este table applied to Colbert 338; shape names fixed on glossed pages 435-438, 453-454, 504.
Five tests against the volume's contemporary glosses (V1-V5): best V2 p. 504, 0.777 characters vs 0.332 (thresholds 0.85/0.75); V4 and V5 not admissible (glosses not literal).
Probable words from a list fixed in advance placed on the training pages only: alpha with a descending tail = f; key K-C01 frozen.
One measurement on held-out p. 523: M5 0.457 vs 0.078 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (gap 0.379); thresholds >= 0.60 and >= +0.30.
Read by sense after a blind shape sheet of 14 questions: 200 words, 146 certain, 31 probable, 1 restored, 22 unresolved (88.5%).
Cryptiana re-read; Favalli 2024 read in full; Favalli's thesis (HAL tel-03435435) not readable; web searches for an edition of fr. 16041-16042 or of this advice: nothing.

outcome.method_basis: Read with Satoshi Tomokiyo's published d'Este table, adjusted on glossed pages of the same volume; the key is partial (one sign e/null open, the code word y unknown) and its test on this page is partial by our protocol.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (certain + probable; restored not counted), counted by script on the word list in reading.md: 200 words, 146 certain, 31 probable, 1 restored, 22 unresolved = 177/200 = 88.5%.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): key frozen, p. 523 transcribed and hashed before decoding, one measurement: M5 0.457 vs 0.078 for the best of 200 shuffled keys; thresholds >= 0.60 and >= +0.30: partial. Earlier tests against the volume's glosses (V1-V5) failed or were not admissible.

Barred dumbbell: e in our key, null in Tomokiyo's table; not settled

texts.label: Colbert 338 p. 523, whole page in cipher
texts.summary: A prince (name in a code word, not read) had the pope asked for the title of king and was refused; he turned to the emperor; the writer was told the emperor alone gave Cosimo of Florence his grand-ducal title; he asks that the King be told and that his source among the pope's people stay secret.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5 Nov 2026 by one AI reader; Brice Dudout answered the shape sheet only. The decryption construes as French sentences with gaps: 146 certain, 31 probable, 1 restored, 22 unresolved of 200 words (88.5%), so read in part.

outcome.notes: The table is Tomokiyo's; key.tsv is given with his credit, our shape names and our few changes marked.

prior.where: The key: S. Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, 'Cardinal d'Este's Cipher (1584-1586)' (henryiii.htm), built on BnF fr. 16041-16042; Colbert 338 not cited, no letter edited. The text of p. 523: no edition found; Favalli, CHMO 49/2 (2024), read, covers 1569-1580 and does not mention it; Favalli's thesis (HAL tel-03435435, 1559-1580) not read in full. Catalogue 1572 open on origin/main (GitHub API, e2315f8a, 5 Nov 2026).

human: Brice Dudout chose the target, set the rules (protocols and amendments hashed before each computation, one measurement on a held-out page, thresholds fixed in advance) and answered the blind shape sheet (shapes only). AI agents transcribed, applied and adjusted the key, measured, read and wrote up. No palaeographer checked the page.
